more.summary: In a study published in Advanced Optical Materials, researchers at Vilnius University (VU) demonstrated perovskite-based laser structures that maintained stable performance over more than 400 million pulses. Their findings address one of the major challenges limiting the practical use of perovskites: their instability.

more.title: Study finds air quality warnings had only a modest impact on Montrealers' movements during wildfires
more.summary: When Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) urged Montrealers to limit outdoor activity during Canada's worst wildfire smoke episodes, the city's travel patterns shifted—but far less than public health officials might have hoped, according to a new McGill University study published in Health & Place.

more.title: Not all rattlesnakes are alike: Research suggests personality influences how rattlesnakes use their venom
more.summary: Imagine encountering a rattlesnake in your backyard or while on a hike. It will most likely "freeze" to avoid attracting attention, but if it feels especially threatened, it may rattle and even strike, delivering a painful dose of venom.

more.title: Hearing laughter may cause orangutans to value rewards more
more.summary: A new study from Indiana University shows that being in a positive mood leads orangutans to value what they learned more strongly. The study comes from the lab of Erica Cartmill, professor of animal behavior, anthropology and cognitive science in the College of Arts and Sciences at IU Bloomington, and was led by Daan Laméris, a postdoctoral researcher at IU.

more.title: Mach9 raises $34M after pivoting to AI CAD software
more.author: Sean O'Kane
more.summary: The startup initially set out to build better, faster, and cheaper surveying hardware in 2021.

more.author: Lee Mohon
more.summary: As part of the agency’s Inspiration Tour, NASA will conduct a flyover at the University of Alabama vs. Texas A&M football game in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, on Saturday, Oct. 24. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F-5 fighter jets during the flyover, highlighting NASA’s contributions to aeronautics and the agency’s continued commitment to […]

more.summary: Agentic AI startup Karta AI has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital…

more.title: Baby manta rays hunker down close to coasts before facing the open ocean's dangers
more.summary: Giant manta rays can grow up to nine meters (30 feet) long with a disk size of seven meters (23 feet) across and weigh up to 2,000 kg (4,400 pounds). This size leaves them with very few natural enemies once they reach adulthood at around eight to 10 years old.

more.title: When powerful women are remembered as witches, we should challenge the historical motive
more.summary: Reclaiming the label "witch" has become an act of feminist solidarity. But are we recovering the women themselves, or a posthumous identity built from accusation rather than fact?

more.title: See Inside Cells Like Never Before in These Vivid Microscopic Images
more.author: Molly Herring
more.summary: Winning entries in the 2026 Nikon Small World competitions reveal the hidden interactions that govern everyday life. The post See Inside Cells Like Never Before in These Vivid Microscopic Images first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: Illegal fishing is thriving in African waters—a satellite system could help change that
more.summary: A patrol boat off the coast of Gabon intercepted three trawlers in July 2026, inside the Grand Sud Reserve. This is one of West and Central Africa's largest marine reserves, where industrial trawling is banned. None of the trawlers held a valid license. The patrol found them because analysts at the nonprofit Global Fishing Watch had studied satellite data and worked out where to look.

more.title: More young people are being recruited as 'money mules' by organized crime groups, new analysis reveals
more.summary: More than 8,900 people aged under 30 were arrested for money laundering offenses in England and Wales between 2020 and 2025. That's more than six in 10 of all money laundering arrests recorded during the period.

more.title: Horror films exploit how human vision works to deliver movies' best scares
more.summary: Imagine you're in the movie theater watching 2018's "Hereditary." During one of the film's most unsettling sequences, the main character, Peter, wakes up in bed disoriented. As he sits up, you hear a couple of gasps from others in the audience. The camera stays locked on Peter as he moves through his house and enters the dim living room.

more.title: How 39 young people experience climate education in a rapidly changing world
more.summary: Ecological grief is growing—and our current approach to climate change education isn't keeping pace.

more.title: Student motivation and responsibility shown to be key to tackling bullying in physical education
more.summary: Physical education has traditionally been one of the most eagerly awaited classes of the school day, since it lets students get out of the classroom, move around and interact with their classmates in a different way—conditions that are conducive to learning values such as camaraderie and cooperation.

more.title: Too much RNA can starve cells of energy, scientists discover
more.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected danger lurking inside cells: too much RNA can damage the structures responsible for producing energy. A new study found that excess RNA, including the normally essential messenger RNA (mRNA), can directly disrupt mitochondria without relying on the immune system. The discovery could help explain how viral infections and certain aging-related diseases damage cells.

more.title: Private business fortunes reveal overlooked source of wealth and inequality in America
more.summary: A majority of Americans blame billionaires for the nation's ever-growing income and wealth divide. But economists Eric Zwick and Owen Zidar say there's a much larger but little-known cadre of very rich folks who may be even more important in closing the gap.

more.title: Virus that sickens cows, kills deer still rare in New York state—for now
more.summary: An insect-driven disease that causes high mortality in white-tailed deer and mimics the symptoms of foot-and-mouth disease in cattle is still rare in New York state, but the warming climate may increase its future spread.
